title: Purple Haze
caption: The HII region DG121, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A soft purple haze with no sharp edges spreads across this picture, with a bright star near the center. This is DG121, a glowing cloud of ionized hydrogen known as an HII region, in the constellation Puppis, the Stern.

HII regions are a kind of emission nebula. They form when young, massive stars give off enough ultraviolet energy to ionize the gas clouds around them, making the gas glow. Their structure tends to be irregular, without crisp boundaries, which gives them their hazy but photogenic look. The brightest star in the region, near the center, is HD 60068.

The image was taken with FORS2 on ESO's Very Large Telescope in the Chilean Atacama Desert. Astronomers have nicknamed it Paranal's Swiss army knife, because it can study many kinds of objects in many different ways. In this case it worked as a camera, recording the nebula through several color filters.

understand.summary: The VLT's FORS2 instrument took this visible-light image through B, V, R and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color mapping isn't published.
filters: 440 nm · Optical B (Very Large Telescope FORS2)

understand.eye: The haze is faint, and the camera's long exposures make it far more visible than it would appear to the eye.

explore: FORS2 stands for FOcal Reducer and low dispersion Spectrograph 2. Besides taking images, it can spread light into spectra, which lets astronomers measure what objects are made of and how they move.
alt: A soft purple haze of glowing gas with a bright star near the center.
